full_judgment:
"The matter would be required to be considered purely from the perspective of the allegation made in the complaint if the allegation is sufficient and specific no benefit can be extended to such Editor-in-Chief. Conversely, it would logically follow that if there are no specific and sufficient allegations, the matter would stand reinforced by reason of the fact that no presumption can be invoked against such Chief Editor or Editor-in-Chief." 

 25. In the instant case the accused petitioner is said to be Chairman of the Editorial board of the 'New Asian Age' news paper in which the alleged libellous report was published. In the complaint petition there is a lump allegation that all the accused persons intentionally published the false report against them but nowhere in the complaint petition, it is stated what role the accused petitioner played in preparation and publication of the report. In the inquiry report submitted by the Police Inspector the accused petitioner was made liable for publication of the report whereas he left out other accused named in the complaint. The reasons stated in the report are simply untenable and cannot justifiably be acted upon only against the accused petitioner. The accused petitioner is admittedly Chairman of the Editorial Board. Unless there is some allegation that he prepared and published the report, it cannot readily be assumed or presumed that he was involved in the publication of the offensive report. As there is no specific and sufficient allegation the matter would stand reinforced of the reason of the fact that no presumption can be drawn against him being Chairman of the Editorial Board. In such view of the matters the order of taking cognizance and issuance of process only against him is an abuse of the process of the court and the proceeding against him is liable to be quashed.
